https://www.thetimes.com/uk/article/m25-.title: M25 to close all lanes during day for first time
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/article/m25-.subtitle: There are five planned closures of the motorway this year, the first from March 15 to allow roadworks between Heathrow and Gatwick
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/article/m25-.text:
A section of the M25 is to close during the daytime for the first time in its history.
Roadworks on a junction between Heathrow and Gatwick airports will force the motorway to shut between junctions 10 and 11 at least five times. The first closure will take place this month.
It will be the first scheduled shutdown affecting all lanes during the day since the motorway around London opened in 1986. Drivers are being warned to expect long delays.
Steve Gooding, director of the motoring research charity the RAC Foundation, said: “For drivers who’ve already had their patience tried by the queues at the Junction 10 works, the phrase ‘you ain’t seen nothing yet’ springs to mind. National Highways’ plea for people to avoid driving in the area applies not just to trips on the M25 but also to those on surrounding local roads on to which the M25 traffic will be diverted.”
Gooding added: “The hope must be that drivers take great care, however frustrating the delays and disruption might be. The last thing we need is shunts or crashes, however minor, because the slightest mishap will compound the misery.”
The five-mile stretch will be closed from 9pm on Friday, March 15 until 6am on Monday, March 18, with a further four closures expected up to September.
Motorists will be forced to detour more than ten miles around northern Surrey while a footbridge over the motorway is demolished and a new gantry is installed. The works are part of a £317 million improvement project to increase the number of lanes around junction 10, and is projected to take three years.
It aims to make it easier for drivers to enter and exit at the interchange — one of the most dangerous motorway junctions.
Jonathan Wade, National Highways project leader, said: “Drivers should only use the M25 if their journey is absolutely necessary. This is the first of five full closures of one of the busiest junctions on our road network. We have spent months planning for these closures and making sure there are diversion routes in place, but there will still be heavy congestion and delays.
“These improvements will bring long-term benefits to drivers who pass through this stretch of the M25, not to mention pedestrians, cyclists and horse riders who will also see positive changes in the area.”
